title: 3-Call Computationally Indifferentiable Iterated Blockcipher
summary: Although statistical indifferentiability is impossible for three or fewer calls, it remains open whether computational indifferentiability is achievable for a 3-call iterated blockcipher under suitable hardness assumptions.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether there exists a 3-call iterated blockcipher that is computationally indifferentiable from an ideal cipher under suitable hardness assumptions, including assumptions based on graph problems or key derivation functions; the achievability of such a construction remains unresolved.

scope.domain: Construction of iterated block ciphers with computational indifferentiability from an ideal cipher.
assumptions: Suitable hardness assumptions, including assumptions based on graph problems or key derivation functions
parameters: 3-call iteration limit for the blockcipher construction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a 3-call iterated blockcipher computationally indifferentiable from an ideal cipher can be constructed under suitable hardness assumptions.

citations.label: Impossibility of Indifferentiable Iterated Blockciphers from 3 or Less Primitive Calls

progress.summary: The source presents computational indifferentiability with three calls as an intriguing constructive direction, suggesting graph-problem or key-derivation-function hardness assumptions may help. It leaves achievability unresolved.
citation_labels: Chun Guo et al., Impossibility of Indifferentiable Iterated Blockciphers from 3 or Less Primitive Calls
